response:
Diagnosis. The winning family is now stable and well identified: MIN(claims-based gross-profit yield, balance-sheet screen) delivers alphas of 4.0-4.5% at t = 3.0-3.4 with FMB slopes near 4.8-5.0. Generation 7 narrowed the mechanism sharply. Industry-demeaning the value leg cut alpha from 4.5% to 1.1%, and demeaning the productivity leg cut it from 3.4% to 1.6%, so the abnormal return lives in *cross-industry* dispersion of both cheapness and asset composition — an FF5-unspanned composition effect, not within-peer stock selection. The earned-buffer conditioner (re/lt) failed at 0.8%, three-year smoothing of the numerator gave no gain, the disjunctive MAX form was weaker (2.9%), and the collected-profit numerator matched but did not beat the incumbent. What remains genuinely unresolved is *what exactly the successful conditioner measures*: (act−lt)/at simultaneously encodes liquidity coverage, current-asset composition and low leverage, three economically different claims that no test has yet separated. With one generation after this one, the highest-value use of this batch is a clean decomposition of the conditioner into its constituent economic content, holding the value leg and the MIN structure fixed, plus one genuinely new conditioner concept (cash runway against the operating cost base) that is scaled by a flow rather than by the balance sheet and therefore cannot be an asset-lightness proxy.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Coverage-ratio conditioned claims value
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(act, lt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: What protects a cheap, profitable firm is the multiple by which its liquid resources cover its obligations, not the size of that surplus relative to its asset base; expressing the screen as a coverage ratio judges a small, liquid firm and a large, liquid firm by the same solvency standard.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The incumbent conditioner (act−lt)/at mechanically rewards firms with small total assets, which is why the critic repeatedly argued it is an asset-lightness proxy rather than a solvency measure; act/lt removes total assets entirely, so if the alpha survives the mechanism is genuinely creditor coverage. It is the single most informative variant to run before the final generation because it determines whether the headline signal should be framed as a solvency screen or an asset-composition tilt.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Current-asset composition conditioned claims value
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(act, at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The screen may have nothing to do with liabilities at all: a cheap, profitable firm whose assets are predominantly current is holding resources that can be redeployed or liquidated quickly, while one whose assets are locked in plant is committed to a business the market has already judged.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This strips the liability term out of the conditioner completely, isolating pure asset composition, and it removes the double liability penalty the critic identified in the incumbent, where lt appears in both the value denominator and the screen. Run alongside Signals 1 and 6 it partitions the incumbent conditioner into coverage, composition and leverage, so whichever performs best defines the economic story for the final consolidated signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Doubly cheap on profit and liquid assets
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The strongest mispricing occurs where both routes to value point the same way: the firm is cheap relative to its profit stream and the market is simultaneously paying little for a balance sheet whose liquid assets already exceed all obligations.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The disjunctive MAX version of exactly these two legs earned 2.9% alpha at t 2.31, establishing that the two routes are partly substitutable; the conjunctive version is untested and asks the opposite question, whether requiring both simultaneously concentrates the mispricing further. Price-scaled net liquid assets is the characteristic behind the archive's largest standalone alpha, so pairing it conjunctively with the value leg that supplies the cross-sectional slope is the natural end-point of that line.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Operating runway conditioned claims value
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), cogs), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Survival is a matter of time, not of ratios: the relevant question for a cheap firm is how many years of its own operating cost base its net liquid resources could fund, because that is the horizon over which it can withstand a demand shock without returning to capital markets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Scaling the net liquid buffer by an annual flow rather than by assets or liabilities produces a runway measured in years, a conditioner that is structurally incapable of being an asset-lightness proxy and that treats a capital-intensive but cash-covered firm as safe. This is the one genuinely new conditioner concept remaining, and because cogs is already in the value leg's numerator the two legs share accounting inputs in a way that ties survival capacity directly to the profit stream being priced.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Persistently solvent claims value
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), at), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A one-year snapshot of liquidity can be engineered by drawing a credit line or stretching payables at the reporting date, whereas a three-year average solvency position reflects a durable financing policy, and only durable solvency should distinguish a bargain from a trap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Averaging was tested on the value leg and gave no improvement, but the conditioner has never been smoothed, and window-dressing of year-end liquidity is a specific, well-documented accounting behaviour that a snapshot screen cannot detect. If durable solvency dominates the snapshot, the final signal should use the averaged screen, which would also reduce annual turnover in portfolio membership and support a higher alpha t-statistic.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Low-leverage conditioned claims value
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(lt, at)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The screen that works may be nothing more than low leverage: a cheap, profitable firm that owes little relative to what it owns has both the staying power and the equity claim on any recovery, regardless of whether its assets happen to be current.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the third and simplest partition of the incumbent conditioner, and it is the only one that does not require current assets to be reported, which lifts coverage from 0.121 back toward 0.14 and mechanically improves the precision of the alpha estimate if the economics are unchanged. A result close to the incumbent would mean the archive's entire asset-side story reduces to leverage, which is the most parsimonious and most implementable conclusion available for the final generation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Coverage-ratio conditioned claims value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The act/lt conditioner is not a monotone transform of the incumbent (act−lt)/at screen and cleanly separates creditor-coverage from asset-lightness, so the diagnostic is legitimate even if the construction is only one denominator away from an existing archive entry.

---CRITIQUE Current-asset composition conditioned claims value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 1
RATIONALE: ZSCORE(WINSOR(act/at)) is an affine transform of ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG((at−act)/at))), so this is a mathematically identical rediscovery of the archived "Cheap and asset-light on the balance sheet" signal (fmb 4.653, alpha 0.037).

---CRITIQUE Doubly cheap on profit and liquid assets---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: MIN of the two legs asks a genuinely different (conjunctive) question than the archived MAX disjunction and uses a price-scaled buffer rather than the asset-scaled one, though it is a modest step and likely highly correlated with the existing 0.045-alpha liquid-backed variant.

---CRITIQUE Operating runway conditioned claims value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Scaling the net liquid buffer by an annual cost flow yields a horizon-based survival screen that is structurally immune to the asset-lightness confound criticized in the incumbent, making this the most substantively new conditioner in the batch; the only caveat is that 1/cogs partly reintroduces a size/turnover tilt.

---CRITIQUE Persistently solvent claims value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A three-year moving average of the identical incumbent conditioner is a cosmetic smoothing variant whose stated motivation (fiscal-year-end window dressing of liquidity) is weakly connected to annual balance-sheet data and is unlikely to change the economic story.

---CRITIQUE Low-leverage conditioned claims value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Book-equity-to-assets as the screen is a defensible parsimony test that also lifts coverage, but note it is a monotone transform of (at−lt)/at and thus close in spirit to the archived equity-funded value work, and its overlap with the lt already in the value denominator means a positive result will be hard to interpret as independent.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cash-quality conditioned claims value
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(che, act), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Not all current assets are equally real: among cheap, profitable firms the safe ones hold their working capital as cash, while those whose current assets are mostly receivables and inventory hold claims that can be written down or discounted exactly when the business deteriorates.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This conditions on composition *within* current assets rather than on the current-versus-fixed split, so it is not an affine transform of the archived asset-light screen and it can rank two firms with identical act/at very differently. It tests a distinct economic claim — that the liquidity screen works because of realizability rather than asset-lightness — which the existing archive cannot answer and which matters for choosing the final headline signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Through-cycle solvency conditioned claims value
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lt)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), at), 5), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The relevant solvency standard is the firm's worst position over a full cycle, not its current one: a cheap firm whose net liquid assets stayed positive even at its five-year trough has demonstrated it can absorb a downturn, whereas one that is liquid today only because it recently raised capital or sold assets has not.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Taking the five-year minimum is a downside-resilience concept rather than a smoothing device — it deliberately ignores good years and scores each firm on its stress point, which is how creditors and distressed-equity investors actually judge staying power. It also separates firms whose current liquidity is a transient consequence of financing activity from those with a durable policy, a distinction the incumbent snapshot screen and any moving average both miss.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
